summary: Jan Beṯ-Şawoce: the supplied English is project machine translation, not an edition translation. All semantic decisions rest on the Turoyo; quoted English is copied from the supplied machine translation.
New root proposal from a single negative relative clause: people are experiencer subjects of ʕaqli. No L-marked experiencer is present, and no overt accusative stimulus is supplied.

mənayye is retained without deciding whether it marks a reflexive domain, a source or another complement. The machine English 'anything' has no separate overt Turoyo noun and is not used to posit valency.
I and Infectum are provisional reader-compatible analyses. No singular Infectum, Preterit, Detransitive or other stem can be recovered from this token; the base-form slots explicitly show the gaps.
Arabic ʕql is a plausible learned/contact comparison, not a verified immediate donor. The surrounding prophetic story does not by itself make the Turoyo relative clause a Syriac quotation.
No light-verb phrase is established: the cognitive predicate is the verb itself.
Confirm I Infectum plural ʕaqli versus a Preterit Intransitive or another learned form; obtain singular Infectum and Preterit before completing the paradigm.
What is the function of mənayye: understand themselves, reason on their own, or another domain? Do not narrow sense1 until resolved.
Is the verb productive Turoyo vocabulary or a learned borrowing confined to this narrative register?
